title: LaRA: Layer-wise rank allocation for efficient fine-tuning of pruned large language models
abstractNote: Structural pruning methods are widely used to compress the size of large language models (LLMs). While the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) technique was proposed to fine-tune pruned LLMs to restore their original performance, it can lead to suboptimal results if distributional differences between layers are not considered. Existing methods attempt to adjust rank values during training or propose a model-specific prediction method to dynamically allocate rank values. However, these methods face challenges in terms of computational resources and generalizability. To address these challenges, we propose LaRA, an automatic framework that profiles the layer features (e.g., information, pruning setting, and position) of pruned LLMs, based on which it provides the optimal rank configuration to better restore performance. Specifically, we design a Rank Allocator to allocate rank configurations according to these layer features, and we train it using a policy-gradient method. To facilitate this, we also propose a Scoring Model that serves as a reward model to predict potential performance. Additionally, we collected approximately 1k real-world rank-performance pairs as our dataset, which were extended through data augmentation, to train these models. We conduct quantitative experiments using different LLMs on seven benchmarks. The results demonstrate that LaRA outperforms existing methods, delivering an accuracy improvement of 2.4 % and a memory reduction of 48.7 % than baselines, indicating that LaRA achieves both better performance recovery and computational resource savings. Furthermore, extended experiments show that LaRA generalizes well across various pruning settings and models. The code and data has been released in https://github.com/yuhua-zhou/LaRA.
